reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm survives the evidence test. A few forms are tempting (e.g. Cd/Ed/Ef/Fb, H2/Hh, and standalone B/F/O/20/W/V), but there is no stable substitution frame where alternating fillers make the same kind of contribution and predict whole meanings compositionally. Shared initial letters or final characters do not yield a consistent paradigm here: for example, d in Cd/Ed/Sd does not have one recoverable meaning, h in Hh/Ch/Dh/Hr is not stable, and digits in H2 and 20 fail the opaque-index test because there is no productive quantity/count contrast in a shared frame. The longer codes (Lk, Pi, Rc, etc.) also do not align compositionally with the standalone symbols by exact reusable morphotactic templates. Therefore the safest analysis is a flat lexicon with all symbols treated as opaque stored entries.
